versions.changelog:
**Fixed**

- On 2019 LG TVs (webOS 4.5), Bonfire did not start at all. [#34]
- With "Ask who's watching on startup" off, there was no Switch Profile button and no way to switch.
- After signing out of the iOS app, the previous account's profile stayed on the sign-in screen and carried over to the next account.
- On iPad, your own profiles could appear as a linked Bonfire, and Manage Profiles asked you to open yourself first.
- The profile picture in the header was drawn zoomed in and blurry.

**Fixed**

- Security: any account could run script in an administrator's browser through the Bonfire settings page. Please update.
- Security: a PIN typed into a TV or app sign-in screen could be guessed with no limit.
- Security: someone using a profile in a browser could take over the main account behind it.
- On Android TV, Roku and other TV apps, choosing a profile and entering its PIN was refused.
- A profile limited to one TV could be missing from that TV's sign-in screen.
- Skipping Quick Connect on known TVs also removed it for other people with the same TV model.
- Signing in on a TV could occasionally fail with a server error.
- Creating a profile could fail with "The supplied value is invalid". [#33]
- The profile picker ran off the bottom of the screen on a TV. [#31]
- A profile kept its old rating after its account's rating was lowered.
- Clearing your PIN, or using the emergency disable code, could stop your password working.
- An account with a PIN could not change its Jellyfin password.
- Creating two profiles at once could go over the profile limit.
- The Signed-in devices list in the dashboard could fail to load.
- The create form showed only four libraries at a time.

**Changed**

- A profile keeps every restriction set on its account, such as remote access, schedules and bitrate.
- Profiles in another household's Bonfire need a PIN, unless their owner allows switching on the home network.
- Hidden Bonfire profiles can no longer be opened.
- Removing someone from your Bonfire changes its code, so they cannot rejoin with the old one.
- Reopening the app keeps the profile you were using. Going back to your main profile asks for its PIN.
- Manage Profiles needs your main profile open.

**Added**

- Thirty starter avatars to pick from, on by default. Turn them off in Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Avatar Library. [#32]
- Picture quality for profile pictures and avatars: Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Picture quality.
- A New code button for your Bonfire.
- A loader for the Samsung Tizen app, so Bonfire updates reach the TV without rebuilding the app. [#16]

**Fixed**

- Giving a profile a new library in Dashboard -> Users was undone the next time anyone entered that profile. Grants made there are now kept. To take a library away from a profile, edit the profile. [#30]
- Turning on "Skip Quick Connect on known devices" took Quick Connect away from apps that already have a password screen. It now applies only to Android TV, which is the one that needs it.

**Added**

- Profiles can appear on the sign-in screens of Jellyfin for Roku, Swiftfin, Findroid and Wholphin, the same as Android TV. Turn off automatic sign in on the app, or it goes straight into the last account.
- Apps that have no user list of their own can enter a profile by typing the profile's name and its PIN.

**Changed**

- The README is shorter. Library artwork, Bonfire sharing and known limitations now have their own pages under docs/.

**Added**

- Profiles can now appear on the sign-in screen of apps that never load the web client, such as Android TV, and be opened with their PIN. New settings under Dashboard -> Bonfire -> TVs & Apps, all off until you turn them on.
- On those screens a profile shows the name you gave it, not the full account name.
- An account that owns profiles can sign in with its PIN as well as its password.
- Apps can be sent straight to the password field instead of a Quick Connect code.
- "Who's watching?" on startup can be set per device instead of everywhere at once.

**Works on Jellyfin 12.0.** The same build serves 10.11 and 12.0 — there is nothing extra to install.

**Fixed**

- On Jellyfin 12.0 the Switch Profile button was missing from the header. Its default layout keeps the old header in the page but hides it, and Bonfire was adding the button there.
- In the profile form, text boxes would not take a click and dropdowns would not open — the page jumped to the top instead. Jellyfin's account menu was being left open, and its focus handling and Bonfire's fought each other.
- The Switch Profile button could appear beside the wrong icon at the wrong size, then move a second or two later. It now appears once, beside your account icon.
- Importing avatars from a folder failed on Jellyfin 12.0, and on any server where an administrator had turned legacy authorization off.
- The Bonfire section on your profile page sat against the left edge while the rest of the page was centred.
- The rename and merge buttons in the device list were unstyled, and drew as empty boxes on televisions without an emoji font.

**Changed**

- Bonfire follows your theme's accent colour on Jellyfin 12.0, which publishes that colour under a new name.

**Fixed**

- Switching to someone's main profile wiped that person's library access, and their sub-profiles' access with it. If this has happened to you, re-tick their libraries in Jellyfin's user settings after updating. [#27]
- Switching into an administrator's account quietly removed their admin rights and hid them from the login screen. [#27]
- Restricting a profile to specific devices could lock it out of every device, including the ones you picked. [#16]
- On a TV, picking a profile changed the name at the top but left you in your main account — same libraries, same Continue Watching, same Next Up. [#16]
- On a TV, moving off the first profile jumped straight to Manage Profiles and no other profile could be reached. [#16]
- On a TV the profile cards had no size and the focus outline never appeared, so nothing looked selectable. Save could also sit below the bottom of the profile form with no way to reach it on a remote. [#16]
- The profile switcher said you were signed in as your main profile even while a sub-profile was in use.
- A profile, device or Bonfire group you had just saved could silently not be there.
- Anything added while the plugin's settings page was open was undone when an administrator pressed Save.
- One computer could appear several times in the device list, and devices that sent no name all read as "Unknown Device".
- Forgetting a profile's only allowed device silently made that profile available everywhere. It is refused now, and says which profiles are in the way.
- "Try again in 15 minutes" after too many wrong PINs. It now tells you the wait it is actually enforcing, which is usually far less.
- Device "last seen" dates reset every time Jellyfin restarted, and the device list never dropped hardware nobody uses any more.
- A language could stop loading until Jellyfin was restarted, dropping everyone back to English.
- Switching profiles on a light theme flashed a black screen, and a switch that went wrong left the screen blank for four seconds.
- The profile screen re-downloaded every profile picture on every page load. Your browser keeps them now.

**Added**

- Bonfire knows when it is on a television, and makes the profile pictures, text and focus outline large enough to use from across a room.
- Rename a device, or tell Bonfire that two entries are the same machine. "Tidy up duplicates" folds together the several devices one browser makes — a profile allowed on any of them stays allowed.
- A list of everyone signed in, with the household each profile belongs to, and a way to sign one device out.
- Export and import the plugin's configuration, so there is a copy of your profiles and PINs somewhere other than one file.
- The audit log can be filtered by name and date, and downloaded.
- Polish, contributed by danis101. [#26]
- TROUBLESHOOTING.md, which answers the most common report first: Bonfire does not edit index.html by default, so a file with no plugin tags in it is a healthy install.

**Changed**

- The Switch Profile button now sits next to your account icon in the header, instead of at the end of the row.
- The interface reads correctly on light Jellyfin themes, where separators and muted text used to be invisible.
- Bonfire does far less work in the background — most noticeable on a TV, and it steps back further while something is playing.
- The "restart to finish updating" notice now names the version running and the version waiting, so you can tell whether your restart worked. [#25]

**New**

- Bonfire no longer edits Jellyfin's `index.html`. The client script is added to the page as it is served, so there is nothing to re-apply after a Jellyfin update and no file permissions to grant. Patching the file stays available as a legacy option under **Advanced → Client script**. (#17, #11, #3)
- The switcher follows your theme's accent colour instead of always drawing Jellyfin blue.
- Profile screens use the whole window on a desktop instead of one phone-width column.
- The picker shows which profile you are currently watching as.

**Fixed**

- On Android, picking a profile could bring the picker straight back, over and over, and a PIN-protected profile could drop you at the account login.
- Picking a profile showed nothing at all for the second or two it takes, so the tap read as missed. The profile you picked now shows a spinner, and the screen no longer goes black while it loads.
- Opening a profile took several seconds and could drop you back on a screen you had already left.
- Bonfire rewrote `index.html` on startup even when set never to touch it.
- The settings page reported the client script as installed whenever the plugin was loaded at all, including on servers where nothing was reaching the page.
- Add Profile was missing from the Manage Profiles screen.
- Library names were cut off to "3D Movi…" when choosing artwork.
- **Upload avatars** and **Upload a folder** were unstyled text instead of buttons.
- "PIN Protected" showed in red and "No PIN" in green — the wrong way round.
- The audit log ran the time into the address as "12:09:28 PMIP".

**Changed**

- The plugin is called **Bonfire** in the Jellyfin sidebar.
- Plugin settings are split into tabs — General, Avatars, Accounts, Activity and Advanced — instead of one page five screens tall.
- Switcher Style and Your Bonfire move out of the profile grid into their own **Settings** screen. Bonfire Grouping is now called Your Bonfire.
- Add Profile appears on Manage Profiles only. The "Who's watching?" screen is people to pick from.
- Setting a profile picture is one panel rather than six controls. The paste-a-URL box is gone: a linked picture could not be cropped, was never stored on your server, and disappeared without warning when the link died.
- Libraries and their artwork are one list, with the artwork controls behind a switch.
- Delete is no longer as prominent as Save.

**New**

- Library artwork can be set per profile. Jellyfin builds a library tile from the items inside it, so a Kids profile could see a poster from a film it cannot open; each profile can now be given its own picture for a library, or none at all. (#19)
- Administrators can set the switcher defaults for the whole server, under Dashboard → Plugins → Bonfire. Anyone who has already chosen keeps their own setting. (#14)
- Avatars can be uploaded several at a time, or a whole folder at once. Administrators with a prepared set already on the server can point at its folder and import it. (#14)
- The profile picker has a Cancel button when you opened it yourself, so you can go back to what you were watching.

**Fixed**

- Switching a profile failed with "Invalid username or password" on Jellyfin 10.11.11, and signed the master account out. (#15)
- On Samsung Tizen, picking a profile changed the avatar but left you in the original account. (#15, #16)
- On a TV, the remote could steer the Jellyfin page hidden behind the Bonfire screen. (#16)
- The TV Back button raised Samsung’s "exit application?" prompt behind the Bonfire screen. Back now steps back one screen instead. (#15)
- "Switch Profile" now appears on the Settings page, not only in the header dropdown. (#14)
- Profile pictures could be zoomed but not dragged.
- Save and Cancel are scrolled into view when a remote reaches them, so long profile forms no longer look frozen. (#15)
- Pictures now load in clients that bundle their own web client, such as Samsung Tizen.
- A missing script tag in index.html now says which of the three causes it is. (#17)

**Changed**

- The emergency disable link appears only once an administrator has set a code.
- Error messages, hints and warnings cut down throughout.

First stable release of the 1.3 line, consolidating the 1.2.x pre-releases. ■ NEW — Tag-based content filtering. Each sub-profile can block or allow content by Jellyfin tag (for example "adults", "teens", "kids"), alongside the existing parental rating limit. Tags are inherited, so tagging a series or a whole library applies to everything inside it, and enforcement happens server-side — meaning it holds on every client, including ones that cannot show the profile switcher at all. Blocked tags are additive with the master account's, and an allow-list can only narrow the master's, so a sub-profile can never see more than its parent. ■ NEW — Reorganised profile editor. Creating and editing a profile is now grouped into four titled sections: Profile (name, colour, picture), Security (PIN, LAN bypass, auto-lock), Libraries, and Content & Device Restrictions. Previously every field sat in one flat list in the order features had been added. Sections are plain blocks rather than collapsible panels so D-pad focus order on TV stays predictable, and the layout adapts to phone widths. ■ NEW — The settings page now lists master accounts with their sub-profiles nested underneath, instead of two separate tables. ■ SECURITY — Fixed a stored cross-site scripting flaw in profile avatar images and colours. Because Bonfire groups render profiles from linked households on each other's switcher screens, a crafted value could run script in another user's browser and steal their session token. Values are now validated on the server and escaped on render. ■ SECURITY — Profile PINs are now stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes rather than unsalted SHA-256, under which a 4-8 digit PIN was recoverable almost instantly from the configuration file. Existing PINs keep working and are upgraded automatically the next time they are entered. ■ SECURITY — An account with no PIN can no longer be switched into from a shared Bonfire, and the local-network PIN bypass no longer applies when stepping into another household's account. Also removed an open redirect on the profile image endpoint. ■ FIX — The dashboard's client-script warnings are now accurate. They re-check index.html on every page load rather than reporting server-startup state, a "Re-check Now" button re-runs the injection without a Jellyfin restart, and the message names the specific cause — including whether Jellyfin can write the file at all. The advisory notice can be dismissed on installs where the file is not writable without elevating. ■ FIX — Permission-fix commands are generated for the account Jellyfin actually runs as, rather than covering every possibility at once. ■ FIX — Editing a profile no longer erases device whitelist entries for devices that are switched off, and the device picker is correctly scoped to your own household. ■ FIX — A saved PIN no longer displays as "No PIN" on your own network, and profile changes appear immediately instead of requiring a page reload. ■ PERFORMANCE — Profile switching no longer rewrites the entire audit log on the request, the client script is served with revalidation so browsers pick up updates on their own, and a listener leak that made the interface progressively less responsive over a session has been fixed.

⚠️ BETA RELEASE — not a finished release; please report issues on GitHub. ▸ Settings page: master accounts and sub-profiles were listed as two separate tables, so working out which profiles belonged to which account meant reading the "Master Account" column on every row. There is now a single list of master accounts, each with its sub-profiles collapsed underneath it behind a "2 sub-profiles" toggle. PIN status and Reset PIN are available at both levels as before. Any sub-profile whose master account no longer exists — normally the residue of a partially failed deletion — is listed separately under "Unlinked sub-profiles" rather than disappearing, so it can still be found and managed. ▸ The permission-fix commands are now generated for the account Jellyfin is actually running as, and the page states which account that is. Previously they had to cover every possibility at once: on Windows, Jellyfin runs either as a service (NT AUTHORITY\NetworkService) or as the signed-in user when installed as a tray/desktop app, so the icacls command granted Modify to ALL local users in order to work in both cases. It now grants access to exactly one account — the real one — which is both less to type and a considerably narrower permission on a file inside Program Files. ▸ The same applies to the Linux and Docker chown commands, which previously assumed the service account was named "jellyfin". That is the convention but not a guarantee, and the commands silently did nothing useful when it was not. If the account cannot be determined, the page falls back to the previous broader commands, so nothing is lost on unusual setups.

New: Tag-based content filtering for sub-profiles. Each profile can now block or allow content by Jellyfin tag (e.g. 'adults', 'teens', 'kids'), matching Jellyfin's own parental-control tag feature. Tags are inherited, so tagging a series or an entire library applies to everything inside it, and enforcement is server-side so it holds on every client. Blocked tags are additive with the master account's and an allow-list can only narrow the master's, so a sub-profile can never see more than its parent. Security: fixed a stored XSS in profile avatar images and colours — these are rendered on other households' switcher screens via Bonfire groups, so a crafted value could steal another user's session token; values are now validated server-side and escaped on render. Security: profile PINs are now stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes instead of unsalted SHA-256 (a 4-8 digit PIN was trivially recoverable from the config file); existing PINs keep working and upgrade automatically on next entry. Security: an account with no PIN can no longer be switched into from a shared Bonfire, and the LAN PIN bypass no longer applies across accounts. Security: removed an open redirect on the profile image endpoint. Fix: the client-script injection now verifies the script is actually present before reporting success — previously an index.html without the expected anchors reported success while the switcher silently never loaded, and the dashboard's failure banner could never appear. Fix: index.html is now written atomically so an interrupted write cannot corrupt the Jellyfin web client. Fix: audit log entries no longer reverse order when trimmed.

Fix: Plugin now loads correctly on Jellyfin 10.11.5. The previous release was compiled against 10.11.6, which caused a loader-level assembly version mismatch (FileNotFoundException on MediaBrowser.Common/Controller/Model) on servers running 10.11.5. Compile target downgraded to 10.11.5 — the plugin remains fully compatible with 10.11.6 and later patch releases.
Release 1.1.0: Codebase cleanup, optimization, documentation updates, and developer API reference alignment.
Initial release.

versions.changelog:
This update brings together 2.0.10.0 and 2.0.11.0 from the beta channel.

If you use the Live TV allow-list behind a reverse proxy: add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings. Without that, every request through the proxy counts as coming from the proxy, and if its address is on your list, everyone gets in. The help text now says so.

Fixed: with Live TV set up on two or more providers, the guide never used your providers' XMLTV files. They were combined into one file that could not be read past the first provider, so the guide always fell back to the simpler per-channel listings and lost categories, ratings and the other details XMLTV carries. Each provider's file is now read on its own. If one provider's file is missing or broken, only that provider's channels fall back, and the others keep their full guide (found and fixed by dillardblom).

Fixed: when two providers used the same guide id for different channels, one of them got no guide, or showed the other provider's programmes. Guide ids are now matched per provider (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: when your provider's XMLTV guide came through cut off part way, building the guide never finished. Each request for the EPG URL kept one CPU core busy until Jellyfin gave up, and the guide stayed empty. A broken file now falls back to fetching the guide per channel, as it already did when the file was missing, and no programme is listed twice (by dillardblom).

Fixed: with Dispatcharr mode on, every sync worker logged in to Dispatcharr at the same time when a sync started. Dispatcharr's login limit refused most of them, and those workers fell back to the Xtream API for the first minutes. There is now one login shared by all of them, and it waits its turn like every other request (reported by dillardblom).

This update brings together 2.0.2.0 to 2.0.9.0 from the beta channel.

If you use Live TV with the Native Tuner only, open the Live TV tab after updating and turn off the new "Publish Playlists" switch. It stays on for anyone who already had Live TV enabled, so an M3U tuner or TiviMate setup keeps working, but the native tuner does not need it.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: a single unreadable value from your provider, such as an empty value where a number belongs, no longer makes content disappear. It could blank a series' title, plot and TMDB id, drop every episode of a series, or make a whole category fail to sync. Such values are now ignored or read as 0, and an item whose ID cannot be read is skipped with a warning while the rest syncs normally (reported by foXaCe).

Fixed: changing Folder Mode, or moving a category to another folder, no longer leaves every moved item in your library twice. The old copies are removed even beyond the orphan safety limit, as long as the item only moved to another category folder; anything that actually disappeared is still protected by the limit. Moved items lose their watched status, because Jellyfin sees a new folder as a new item (reported in andreadegiovine's fork).

Fixed: when orphan cleanup removes a movie or series, the NFO and poster the plugin wrote are removed with it, so the folder no longer stays behind. Files you added yourself, such as subtitles or your own NFO, are kept, and so is the folder (idea from andreadegiovine).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

New: with "Fallback to Year-Free Lookup" on, an unmatched movie is also searched with the year of the provider's release date and with its original title, which helps when the title carries the wrong year or is in another language. A search without a year is checked against the release date, so it cannot pick a remake. A match found by the year-free retry is now remembered for later syncs, for movies and series. Movies already in your library keep their folders (idea from philx17).

New: "Publish Playlists" on the Live TV tab. The M3U and Catch-up M3U URLs contain your Xtream username and password and can be reached without a Jellyfin login. They are now only served while this switch is on, and it is off when you enable Live TV from now on. The EPG URL and channel logos are not affected (proposed by dillardblom).

New: "Restrict These URLs To" limits the Live TV URLs to the addresses you list, one per line. Leave it empty for no restriction. If you use it, include 127.0.0.1 and ::1, since Jellyfin fetches channel logos itself, and behind a reverse proxy add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings first (written by dillardblom).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

This update brings together 1.55.1.0 to 1.55.3.0 from the beta channel.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

Categories load their items again on Jellyfin 12 (#117).

Jellyfin 12 stops accepting the legacy `X-Emby-Token` request header. Two of the configuration page fetch sites still sent it: the Live TV category loader and the Series / VOD content loader. Both now send `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=` instead, which Jellyfin 12's `CustomAuthentication` middleware expects. The Test connection button was never affected and still works as before. Two-line header swap in `config.js`, no server-side change.

Test Dispatcharr now tests the password you just typed.

Typing a Dispatcharr API password and pressing Test before saving tested the password that was already saved, not the one on screen. It came back red with "authentication failed" for credentials that were perfectly correct, and nothing suggested that saving first would change the answer. Type, test, save once it goes green is the obvious way to use a test button, and that order never worked.

It now sends what is on the form, the way the Test Connection button above it always has. Clearing the Dispatcharr URL and pressing Test now tests the Xtream address, which is what leaving that field empty means, instead of quietly putting the old URL back.

A provider you are setting up for the first time can be tested as well. Before, with nothing saved yet, it answered "Please configure Base URL first" about a Base URL sitting on screen in front of you.

Nothing else changed, and catch-up, syncing and Live TV are untouched.

The last of your provider password is out of the Live TV playlist.

1.53 replaced every stream URL in LiveTv.m3u and Catchup.m3u with a Dispatcharr address that needs no credentials. One thing still carried the password: the catch-up attribute on channels that have an archive. That attribute is a template your IPTV app fills in and plays by itself, so it has to work on its own, and the only address that does is the one with your username and password in it. Dispatcharr has a catch-up address of its own, but it refuses callers who have not logged in, and these playlists are deliberately served without a Jellyfin login so that Jellyfin's own tuner can read them. There was nothing safe to put there, so the attribute is now left out.

What this changes for you: nothing, if you watch catch-up in Jellyfin. Those channels still have their archive and still play the same way. If you point an external IPTV app at these playlists, that app will no longer offer catch-up on those channels. If you would rather have it back, there is a new setting under Catch-up / Timeshift that puts the attribute in again, with the warning that it carries your password.

Measured on a live setup before and after: 720 channels, 63 lines with the password in them, now none.

Also fixed: the line in the log that tells you how much of the playlist still carries credentials only appeared on the rare occasions the plugin fetched the channel list fresh. It now appears whenever a playlist is built, which is when you would actually go looking for it.

Your provider password is no longer in the Live TV playlist.

If you run Dispatcharr in front of your provider, the M3U the plugin serves now points at Dispatcharr's own channel addresses instead of building URLs with your Xtream username and password in them. Those URLs have always been reachable without a Jellyfin login, on purpose, because Jellyfin's own tuner cannot send one, which meant anyone who had one of those links also had your provider account. Measured on a real setup: 720 of 720 channels, every stream address credential free, where before every single line carried the password.

A channel Dispatcharr does not recognise keeps its old address rather than disappearing from your guide, and the log says how many did and that those lines still carry credentials. Without Dispatcharr nothing changes at all.

One part is not done yet. Channels with a catch-up archive carry a separate address for replaying past programmes, and that one is a template other apps fill in themselves, so it still has your credentials in it. On the setup this was measured against that is 63 lines out of 720. Finishing it needs checking how Dispatcharr expects a time to be expressed, which has not been verified, so it was left rather than guessed at.

Also fixed: with Dispatcharr on a different address than your provider, movie links were pointed at the wrong one of the two.

Channels that would not direct play, and quicker metadata behind Dispatcharr.

Fixed: if your provider does not send stream statistics, every channel arrived at your player with nothing to say what it actually was. Players refused them as an unsupported format, and the server re-encoded pictures they could have shown as they were, without graphics acceleration because it did not know what it was decoding either. Jellyfin can work this out by looking at the stream, and the plugin was accidentally stopping it from looking. Channels from providers that do send statistics are unchanged. One trade-off worth knowing: if the inspection fails, Jellyfin now assumes the picture is interlaced and smooths it, which is slower than before, where the plugin simply asserted it was not (diagnosed by pemontto).

Changed: with Dispatcharr Mode on, film and series descriptions, cast, ratings and artwork now come from Dispatcharr directly instead of going the long way round through its Xtream compatibility layer. Series episodes had no Dispatcharr route at all until now. Anything that does not answer falls back to the old route, so a Dispatcharr too old to have these endpoints keeps working exactly as before, and with Dispatcharr Mode off nothing changes at all (contributed by dillardblom).

Radio channels, and a plainer warning about the Live TV setup URLs.

Fixed: radio stations were published as ordinary television channels. Providers mark them with a stream type that the plugin read and then ignored, so they ended up in the TV list with everything else. The playlist now flags them as radio, which is what players like Kodi use to put them under Radio, and the built-in tuner reports them as radio to Jellyfin, which keeps radio in its own section. Only the one value that is known to mean radio counts: providers use that same field for their own bookkeeping, and guessing would move real television channels out of the TV list, which is harder to recover from than a radio station in the wrong place. If you run Dispatcharr in front of the plugin you will not see a difference, because it reports every channel as ordinary live TV (reported by dillardblom).

The three setup URLs on the Live TV tab now say what they are. They work without a Jellyfin login, on purpose, because Jellyfin's own tuner and guide fetcher do not send one when they fetch them. What was never spelled out is what that means: Xtream has no token or session, so your provider username and password sit in every stream line of the playlist, and anyone who can reach one of those URLs has your account. The settings page, the README and the developer notes now all say so, along with the two things that limit it: keeping those URLs off the open internet, and using the built-in tuner, which never publishes a playlist at all (raised by dillardblom).

Watch programmes that have already aired.

New: a Xtream Catch-up entry under Channels. Pick a channel, pick a day, and play something that has already been on. Jellyfin's own Live TV cannot do this at all: its player refuses any programme once its end time has passed, and there is no setting anywhere to change that. This sits beside Live TV rather than replacing it, so live viewing and recording keep working exactly as they do now.

It is off until you switch it on. You need Enable Catch-up, which you may already have on for other apps, plus the new Watch catch-up inside Jellyfin. Only channels your provider keeps an archive for appear, and only for as many days back as that provider actually keeps.

Some providers publish only what is coming and never what has been, so a day that has passed lists nothing even though the recording plays perfectly well. Those days are offered in blocks of time instead, so you pick half past eight on Saturday rather than a title. Channels that do publish a proper guide show programme names as you would expect.

Providers disagree about what time it is, and asking for the wrong hour would quietly give you the wrong programme with no error. The plugin now asks your provider what time it thinks it is and requests the recording for the hour it actually aired. If a provider answers that wrongly there is a correction setting under Catch-up.

Fixed: the catch-up day limit on the settings page refused anything above 14, while the server has always accepted up to 30 (raised by dillardblom in the same discussion).

Name your providers, a connection test that says what is actually wrong, and a settings page that stops breaking after you remove a provider.

New: providers can be given a name. The dropdown at the top of the settings page listed them as Provider 1, Provider 2 and so on, which tells you nothing once you have more than a couple of accounts configured. There is a Name field on the General tab now, and the list updates as you type. Leave it empty and it goes back to numbering them, so nothing changes if you do not use it (suggested by dillardblom).

Fixed: removing a provider could leave the Add Provider button dead, with nothing happening when you clicked it and a page refresh not helping. Moving around the Jellyfin dashboard rebuilds the settings page in place, and being rebuilt a second time made it fail before any of its buttons were connected (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: Test Connection answered every bad address with the same sentence about needing http:// in front, even when the address on screen looked perfectly normal. It now shows the value it could not read, and tells you when the address you typed is not the address it would actually contact. That last one is the case you cannot see: an invisible character or a lookalike letter copied in from a provider's web page quietly turns the host into something else (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: the Live TV instructions told you to add the playlist address as an HDHomeRun tuner, which does not work. It is an M3U Tuner. The three addresses under Setup URLs belong in three different places, one of which is not Jellyfin at all, and each line now says where it goes. The Xtream Library entry that appears in Jellyfin's own tuner list is explained as well (reported by dillardblom).

Also: the option that groups films sharing a TMDB id now says how to apply it to films already in your library, and what that costs you (raised by andreadegiovine).

Playback failures from a stray space, lost artwork on multi-version films, Dispatcharr logins, and two new grouping options.

Fixed: a password saved with a space before or after it was used exactly as typed, so every stream URL came out malformed and playback failed with a 403 on every single item; both password fields are now trimmed and configurations already saved are corrected too, so nothing needs re-entering (reported by jamillejh). Films your provider carries as V1, V2 and V3 all write to one information file, and they were written at the same time without coordination, so they could overwrite each other and a version whose details could not be fetched would replace a complete file with an empty one; this became visible in 1.47.0.0, which is what put real content in those files, and the version with actual information now wins whichever one finishes first (reported by andreadegiovine). Dispatcharr mode had no address of its own, so the login went to your Xtream server, which has no such page and answers "not found"; there is now a Dispatcharr URL field, and leaving it empty keeps the old behaviour of using the Xtream address (reported by jght2). New: an option to put the category in front of Live TV channel numbers, so a guide built from several categories stays grouped instead of interleaved, which also stops two channels sharing a number and one of them becoming unreachable (requested by dulfer). And a per-provider option to write copies of a film that your provider reports under the same TMDB id into one folder, so Jellyfin shows them as versions of one film; only ids your provider supplies are grouped, never ones found by searching on the title, so a film and its remake cannot be merged by accident (requested by andreadegiovine). Both new options are off by default and neither moves or renames anything already in your library. (#83, #84, #86, #88, #90)

Your movies and shows arrive with descriptions, cast and artwork.

Until now the plugin wrote almost nothing alongside each file it created: a title, a year and an ID. Anything Jellyfin's own metadata providers could not identify therefore sat in your library as a bare entry with no poster and no synopsis. Your provider was already sending the plot, genre, cast, director, country, rating, release date, trailer and poster and backdrop images, and the plugin was discarding all of it. That information is now written into the files Jellyfin reads. Posters and backdrops are referenced straight from your provider, so nothing extra is downloaded to your server. Anything Jellyfin can identify on its own is unaffected, its own metadata still takes priority, and any field your provider leaves empty is simply left out rather than written blank. Items also carry the date your provider added them, so Recently added reflects the provider's catalogue; providers report that date in two different formats and both are now understood. Contributed by @andreadegiovine. (#87)

Switching a provider back to Single folder mode keeps your category ticks.

If you had a provider set to Multiple folder mode and switched it back to Single, the category list came back with every box unticked, even though your categories were still configured. Saving from that screen wrote an empty selection, and an empty selection means "sync everything", so a setup meant to cover a handful of categories quietly pulled in the provider's entire catalogue. The list now comes back with the categories you had assigned to your folders already ticked.

This only affected configurations last saved on 1.44.0.0 or earlier. If you have saved your settings on 1.45.0.0 or later, you were never exposed to it.

Sync every Live TV channel except the categories you pick.

Live TV used to offer two choices: take every channel your provider has, or tick the categories you want one by one. The second option meant that whenever your provider added a new category, you silently missed it until you happened to notice and tick it. There is now a third option, "Sync all channels EXCEPT the categories you tick". Tick the handful you never watch and everything else comes through, including any category your provider adds later. Tick nothing and you get everything. Movies and Series already worked this way; Live TV now matches them. Per-channel exclusions work in the new mode too, so you can still drop individual channels from the categories you are keeping.

Saving the config page could wipe your Live TV category selection. If you opened the plugin settings and saved before the category list had finished loading, or without loading it at all, your selection was quietly replaced with an empty one. In the "pick specific channels" mode that meant no channels synced at all. Your saved selection is now left alone unless the list is actually on screen.

Live TV could fail to load channels on some providers. Providers report which categories a channel belongs to in several different formats, and anything other than the most common one caused the whole channel fetch to fail rather than just that one field, which could take out Live TV entirely. All the known formats are now accepted.

Multiple folder mode with no categories assigned now syncs nothing instead of everything.

IF YOU USE MULTIPLE FOLDER MODE, READ THIS. Previously, a provider set to Multiple folder mode with no categories assigned to any folder synced the provider's ENTIRE catalogue into the root of your library, because an empty selection was read as "no filter". It now syncs nothing and tells you why. If your sync suddenly does nothing after upgrading, that is this change: assign categories to your folders, or switch Folder Mode back to Single (which still means "sync everything"). Your existing files are not deleted - orphan cleanup refuses to run when the selection resolves to nothing.

Blocked orphan cleanup is no longer invisible. When cleanup is skipped because the deletion ratio exceeds the safety threshold, the sync used to report success with zero deletions and zero errors, identical to a healthy run. The counts are now on the sync result, the Last Sync panel shows them with a warning, and the run says so at the end instead of in a single log line thousands of entries earlier.

The config page refuses to save a Multiple folder mode provider with no categories assigned, and can no longer wipe a saved folder configuration when the category list has not loaded.

Known issue: switching folder mode from Multiple back to Single repaints the category list but does not restore the ticks, so check your selection before saving in that case. Tracked in issue #81.

Nearly all of this release comes from @andreadegiovine, who reported the problems, found the causes and wrote the code. BEFORE YOU UPDATE: movie folders carrying a version tag are renamed, so "Movie Name [V1]" becomes "Movie Name" and all versions of a film sit together. The old folders become orphans and are removed on your next sync if Clean up orphaned files is on, taking watched status and any artwork in them with it. If a large share of your library carries those tags the rename can exceed the Orphan Safety Threshold, in which case cleanup is skipped and you will see both old and new folders until you raise it. New: movie and series category pickers get an Include / Exclude selector, so you can tick the categories you do not want and have everything else sync, including categories your provider adds later. Duplicate copies of a film tagged V1, V2 and similar now group into one entry with a version dropdown instead of appearing as separate movies. The Orphan Safety Threshold is now editable in the plugin settings instead of only in the configuration file on the server. Fixed: when a provider offered the same film twice with the same quality tag, the second copy silently replaced the first with nothing logged and no error reported, and which copy survived could change between syncs. The same applied to episodes sharing a season and episode number. (#74, #76, #80)

Adds a per-provider Request Timeout setting under Performance. Providers with very large catalogs could not answer within the fixed 100 second limit, which failed the whole channel, movie or series fetch. Timeouts are now retried, and the error says the request timed out instead of reporting it as cancelled. Live TV also starts faster after a restart: the channel list is served from local storage while it refreshes in the background, instead of making Jellyfin wait for a full download from your provider. Also fixes release builds reporting the wrong version number under Dashboard > Plugins. (#73)
fix: repair incomplete series folders during incremental sync — verifies snapshot entries have actual .strm files before skipping them, preventing orphaned folders with only metadata (#65, fixes #64)
feat: multi-provider Live TV support — configure multiple Xtream providers simultaneously for Live TV channels (#63, closes #56)

Channel Overrides now accept an optional 4th field: StreamId=Name|Number|LogoUrl|Tags (comma-separated). Tags are applied to Live TV channels and can be used for Jellyfin access control (show/hide channels per user). See PR #61.

Fix duplicate series folders when TVDB/TMDB ID lookup fails (rate limited, timeout, or no match). The plugin now reuses the existing named folder instead of creating a duplicate with no identifier suffix.

Live TV channels are now grouped by their Xtream category. Each channel is tagged with its provider category, so the Jellyfin Live TV guide shows category groups instead of one flat list. Applies to native tuner (ChannelGroup) and M3U/XMLTV (group-title).
Channel Override logos can now be a local file path (e.g. /media/logos/fox.png), not just an http(s) URL. The plugin serves local logos over HTTP. Resolves #53.
Adds per-item selection for Movies and Series, matching Live TV per-channel selection. Expand a Movie or Series category to enable or disable individual titles. Resolves #54.

Adds an in-Jellyfin 'Use beta channel' toggle under Dashboard > Plugins > Xtream Library > Settings > General > Updates. When enabled, the plugin registers its beta plugin manifest URL with Jellyfin's plugin repository list so pre-release versions appear in Dashboard > Plugins > Catalog like any other plugin. Disabling removes the entry. State persists across Jellyfin restarts. This release also rolls up everything previously available only on the beta channel between v1.34.0.0 and v1.36.6.0: multi-provider config UI improvements (#36), live-stream date parsing fixes (#41), three EPG XMLTV parsing bugs (#45), legacy-config recovery for users orphaned by the v1.33.3.0 GUID change (#49), Native Tuner UI duplicate-channel warning (#50), multi-provider Live TV URL construction fix (#46), and Live TV channel counts on the sync status dashboard (#48). See https://github.com/firestaerter3/Jellyfin-Xtream-Library/releases for full per-version notes.

Adds a direct 'Xtream Library' entry to the Jellyfin admin dashboard sidebar (#36, thanks @dwizzle204). Sets EnableInMainMenu = true on the embedded config page so the sidebar surfaces an Xtream Library entry directly under Dashboard > Plugins, alongside the existing Dashboard > Plugins > Xtream Library path. Pure UX improvement, no functional change. Cherry-picked from the original PR with author credit preserved via Co-Authored-By, the original PR's new PluginTests.cs collided with the unrelated test file added for BUG-009, so the sidebar-registration assertion is now an additional test on the existing PluginTests.cs.

Fixes live-stream list fetch failures on Xtream providers that return the 'added' field as a formatted date string (e.g. '22/05/2024 10:00:00') instead of a Unix timestamp (#41, thanks @gamegninou). LiveStreamInfo.Added was previously typed as long, which forced strict integer JSON deserialization and threw JsonSerializationException for the entire live-stream list whenever the provider used the string variant. The field has zero readers in the codebase, it only exists for round-trip JSON purposes, so the loosest type that accepts every provider variant is right. Changed to string, matching the sibling StreamInfo.Added (VOD movies) which has always been a string. Intentionally simpler than the converter-based approach proposed in #41, which tried MM/dd before dd/MM and would have silently mis-parsed ambiguous dates with day ≤ 12. 4 new deserialization tests.

Recovers configuration for users who lost their plugin settings across the v1.33.3.0 GUID change (#49). Some users who upgraded from v1.31.44.0 (the [MOVED] shim) to v1.33.3.0+ (the new GUID build) ended up with their pre-v1.32 settings (BaseUrl, folder mappings, etc.) orphaned in a sibling XML file while the new plugin started against an empty in-memory config. The existing migration only operated on what Jellyfin had already loaded, so the orphan was never recovered. This release adds a constructor-time importer that runs before the existing migration: when the in-memory config looks completely fresh, scan the configurations directory for two known historical config filenames our plugin has ever written, validate each candidate against a schema sentinel (folder mappings or TMDb/TVDb override maps populated) that distinguishes our schema from the upstream Kevin Jilissen Jellyfin.Xtream plugin's, copy the legacy fields in, and rename the chosen orphan to .migrated-<date>.bak so it is not picked up on next boot. Defensive: strict trigger gate (only fires when Providers is empty AND BaseUrl is empty AND folder mappings are empty); schema sentinel prevents credential cross-pollination if both plugins are installed side-by-side; orphan is renamed not deleted, preserving an audit copy; rename failure is non-fatal because the import already succeeded in memory. Third installment of the multi-provider migration story (v1.33.1.0 fixed endpoint gating, v1.33.2.0 fixed the pre-v1.32 startup migration, v1.36.1.0 fixed URL construction, this fixes the case where the migration target file is not the file the user's data is in). No configuration change required.

Fixes three distinct EPG parsing bugs (#45, thanks @FilipBB). (1) XmlReader double-advance: AppendUpstreamProgrammes used XNode.ReadFrom inside a while(reader.Read()) loop, which advances the reader twice per element. For minified XMLTV (no whitespace between programme tags) every other programme was silently skipped from the guide. (2) Offset parsing failure on +HH:MM style offsets: TryParseXmltvTime only accepted +HHMM. Modern XMLTV providers that use the ISO 8601 style with a colon (e.g. +02:00) had their programmes parsed as UTC and filtered out as in-the-past. (3) Aggressive past-filter dropped currently-playing shows: any programme ending even a second before now was discarded, so minor clock skew between provider and server made the now-playing show disappear from the guide. Now: 1-hour grace period. Also: extra date format support (YYYYMMDDHHMM and YYYYMMDD as accepted alternatives) and 7 new tests covering offset forms and short date formats. Follow-up marks TryParseXmltvTime as internal so the tests can call it directly instead of via reflection.

Clarifies the Enable Native Tuner UI to prevent duplicate Live TV channels (#50). The previous checkbox description told users to add the Xtream Library tuner manually under Dashboard > Live TV > Tuner Devices, but Jellyfin does not show ITunerHost-based tuners there (that list is only for manually-added tuners). Users who followed the instruction and also pasted the M3U URL as a manual HDHomeRun tuner ended up with both code paths publishing the same channel set, hence every channel appearing twice in the guide. This release replaces the misleading instruction with an accurate one, adds a 'Pick one tuner mode' warning inline under the Native Tuner checkbox explicitly calling out the duplicate-channels symptom, notes the transcoding-vs-remux trade-off so users can choose the right mode for their hardware, and adds a matching warning in the Setup URLs section so the cross-reference is visible from either entry point. No tuner code change; both modes remain fully supported.

Fixes Live TV playback on multi-provider configs (#46 follow-up). Users who configured their provider exclusively via the multi-provider UI (introduced in v1.32) were getting unplayable channels because the M3U export and native tuner both emitted stream URLs shaped like /live///{streamId}.ts — no scheme, no server, no credentials. FFmpeg refused with 'No such file or directory'. Cause: BuildStreamUrl and BuildCatchupUrl were the last consumers still reading the legacy single-provider config fields directly; on a fresh v1.32+ install those fields are empty and only Providers[0] is populated. Fix: a new ResolveLiveTvProvider helper resolves credentials from Providers[0] first (falling back to legacy fields for any config caught mid-migration), and all three URL builders route through it. Third installment of the multi-provider migration story (v1.33.1.0 fixed endpoint gating, v1.33.2.0 fixed the pre-v1.32 startup migration, this fixes URL construction). No configuration change required.

Live TV channel counts on the sync status dashboard (#48). After each sync, the dashboard panel now shows a Live TV row with the total channel count and added/updated/deleted split, matching the existing Movies and Series rows. The same counters appear in the live progress display while a sync is running. How it works: at the end of SyncAsync the plugin fetches the current channel set, compares it against a persisted JSON snapshot (live-tv-channels.json in the plugin data folder), and writes the new snapshot back. A channel counts as 'updated' when its name, EPG channel id, logo URL, or channel number differs. The M3U/EPG cache is invalidated as part of the refresh so Jellyfin's next tuner poll sees the new data. A Live TV refresh failure no longer aborts the sync — VOD/Series counts persist and the error message is surfaced separately. First sync after upgrade shows every channel as 'added' because no previous snapshot exists yet.

Live TV channel checkboxes track parent category state (#46 follow-up). After clicking the master Deselect All button in Pick mode, expanding any (now-deselected) category showed every channel underneath as ticked, even though those channels would not actually sync. Cause: per-channel checkbox state was computed purely from the excludedLiveStreamIds list, and v1.35.0.0's correct decision to clear that list on master Deselect All collapsed the rendering logic to 'all channels checked because nothing is excluded'. Fix: channel checkboxes now gate on the parent category checkbox as well, render unchecked with an italic hint when the parent is deselected, auto-tick the parent when the user re-enables an individual channel or panel-level Select All, and re-render any expanded child panel immediately when the category checkbox flips. No configuration change required.

Truncate STRM filenames to 255 bytes (fixes #47). Series with very long episode titles (e.g. one Interspecies Reviewers episode whose provider-supplied title runs to 240+ characters) silently failed to sync because the resulting STRM filename exceeded Linux's NAME_MAX per-component cap, throwing PathTooLongException on every sync attempt. The episode and movie filename builders now run their output through a UTF-8 byte-aware truncation step that preserves the .strm extension, respects multi-byte character boundaries (Japanese, emoji, etc.), and trims trailing separator punctuation introduced by the cut. 255 bytes is the cross-platform safe ceiling — Windows NTFS and macOS APFS use 255 UTF-16 code units which is laxer. No configuration change required.

Live TV channel selection overhaul (fixes #46). Three intertwined bugs are fixed: (1) category-level Deselect All now actually drops per-channel exclusions; (2) empty category selection no longer means 'sync all' — there is now an explicit Sync ALL vs Pick specific channels mode toggle; (3) new top-of-list toolbar (Select all / Deselect all / Clear channel exclusions), live counter, and client-side category search make handpicking a small subset fast. Existing configs with populated Live TV selections are auto-migrated to Custom mode to preserve behavior. Fresh installs stay on Sync ALL by default. Heads-up: configs with channel exclusions but no category selection land on Custom + empty selection (= zero channels) — click 'Select all' if that is not what you want.

Preserve full EPG metadata from upstream XMLTV (fixes #42): the plugin previously generated XMLTV from Xtream's JSON endpoint which only exposes title and description. It now passes the upstream xmltv.php through verbatim, preserving categories, ratings, credits, icons, dates, and star-ratings. Jellyfin can again categorize Live TV programs by genre. Falls back to the old JSON-based fetch if the upstream XMLTV is unavailable.

Fix overlapping plugin GUID (#43): the boilerplate placeholder GUID a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890 was shared with three unrelated Jellyfin plugins. Replaced with a freshly-generated random GUID. NOTE: existing installs are treated as a different plugin after upgrade — uninstall the old 'Xtream Library' entry from Jellyfin and reinstall to pick up this version. Plugin configuration is preserved across the reinstall. This release also rolls up multi-provider support (v1.32.0.0), per-channel Live TV selection (v1.33.0.0), and Live TV / legacy-config migration fixes (v1.33.1.0, v1.33.2.0) from the beta channel.

versions.changelog: ⚠️ This plugin has moved to a new GUID. You won't see future updates on this entry. After updating, open the plugin catalog and install 'Xtream Library' (it will appear as a separate entry with the new GUID), then uninstall this plugin and restart Jellyfin. Provider settings, library folders, and channel selections carry over automatically. See https://github.com/firestaerter3/Jellyfin-Xtream-Library/issues/46 for context.

Fix legacy-config migration silently failing on upgrades from pre-v1.32 releases. The [Obsolete] attribute on the legacy single-provider fields caused .NET's XmlSerializer to skip them during deserialization, so the on-startup migration into Providers[0] never ran. After this fix the existing provider settings are picked up on first restart. Pairs with v1.33.1.0's Live TV credential-check fix.

Fix connection test crash when provider returns "N/A" for active_cons or max_connections: some Xtream providers send non-numeric strings for these user info fields, which now fall back to 0 instead of throwing a deserialization error (fixes #39).

Add regex removal patterns for STRM file names: new 'Regex Removal Patterns' config field (alongside the existing substring 'Custom Title Removal Terms') applies to file names only, leaving folders untouched so Jellyfin metadata providers keep [tmdbid-N] / [tvdbid-N] identification (closes #32).

name: QualityGate [✓✓]
overview: Cap the resolution a user may be served, measured against the media's actual height.
description:
Quality Gate lets Jellyfin administrators cap the resolution a user may be served. The cap is measured against the media's actual height, read from its video stream, so it holds whatever the file is called. Media above the cap is served as a capped transcode, or as a lower-resolution version of the same item where one exists, and requests for the original file are refused. Useful for bandwidth management and tiered access.

- Add recording controls to the grouped web EPG. Users with Jellyfin's Live TV management permission can schedule, edit and cancel single-program or series timers, including padding and series options; recording errors remain visible in the dialog.

versions.changelog: v0.2.0.2: Jellyseerr person passthroughs

### 0.2.0.1
Revert the 0.2.0.0 web UI takeover — the injected `/jellyfish/ui/home.js` script triggered a browser HTTP Basic auth prompt on the Jellyfin login page and locked users out of the web client.
- Removes the FileTransformation registration and all injected ES modules.
- Returns to the 0.1.0.6 bridge-only behaviour (Jellyseerr/Radarr/Sonarr passthroughs).

v0.2.0.0

Add a full web UI takeover that ports the Jellyfish mobile home page to jellyfin-web.

- Inject custom ES modules into Jellyfin's web client via `jellyfin-plugin-file-transformation`.
- Render a hero carousel, Jellyseerr discovery rails (trending, popular, watchlist, watch providers, genre sliders, 5 mood rails, history-seeded recommendations), Radarr/Sonarr upcoming rails, and native Jellyfin rails (continue, next up, latest, per-library).
- Add a Seerr request modal with season selector (POSTs to `/jellyfish/jellyseerr/request`).
- Hide native Jellyfin home sections except the library shortcuts row.
- Style matches the Flutter mobile app (Fraunces / Fira Code / Inter, dark palette, pill chips).
- Includes a deploy-local fix: stop the container before swapping the plugin directory to avoid Jellyfin marking the plugin as missing.

Requires `jellyfin-plugin-file-transformation` to be installed on the target Jellyfin server (manifest: https://www.iamparadox.dev/jellyfin/plugins/manifest.json).

Add Jellyseerr `movie/{id}/similar` and `tv/{id}/similar` passthroughs so the "Because you watched…" rail can resolve.
- Both forward the full incoming query string (page, language, …).

Forward full query string on Jellyseerr discover passthroughs.
- `discover/movies`, `discover/tv`, `discover/watchlist` now forward every query param (sortBy, voteCountGte, voteAverageGte, genre, watchRegion, watchProviders, …) instead of only `page`.
- Remove `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/config`: exposing the admin X-Api-Key to authenticated clients is no longer needed now that the passthrough is transparent.

Add `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/config` — returns the configured Jellyseerr URL and admin API key to authenticated callers so the mobile client can hit `/api/v1/discover/...` directly with the full TMDB query surface (sortBy, voteCountGte, voteAverageGte, …). 503 when the plugin isn't configured.

Add Jellyseerr proxy endpoints to eliminate client 404s:
- `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/watchproviders/movies` (optional `?watchRegion=`)
- `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/watchproviders/tv` (optional `?watchRegion=`)
- `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/genreslider/movie`
- `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/genreslider/tv`
- `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/discover/watchlist` (optional `?page=`)

Also fixes the release workflow so the per-version changelog actually comes from the tag annotation (jprm has no `--changelog` flag, and `actions/checkout` needs an explicit fetch to preserve annotated tag objects).

## 兼容性说明

为了避免升级 Jellyfin 12 后可能与 Jellyfin 10.11 不兼容的情况，保留此版本作为 Jellyfin 10.11 的最后一个版本。

后续插件将不再考虑 Jellyfin 10.11 的兼容性，若出现不兼容情况，可以下载此版本。

## 新功能与改进

- 增加按用户管理 Bangumi 授权，以及 NSFW 播放记录的私密上报选项。
- 增加缺失 Bangumi ID 的补全工具和 `bangumi.ini` 媒体库管理功能，改进批量选择及刷新反馈。
- 增加动画搜索偏好和优先使用原始标题搜索的配置，支持自定义 Bangumi 网站地址。
- 引入 Anitomy 剧集解析器，改进文件名、集数和多季度识别。
- 增强音乐元数据与播放记录同步，调整插件设置页面。

## 问题修复

- 修复 Bangumi 图片地址和搜索结果处理问题。
- 修复剧集与季度未读取 `bangumi.ini`、未知季度和重复剧集扫描中的特别篇识别问题。
- 修复音乐刮削中的元数据丢失及艺人类型筛选问题。
- 修复 infobox 解析死循环及重复字段处理。
- 改进异步请求、取消操作、评分刷新和播放状态缓存处理。

Release 2.0.0.12
AniLiberty STRM Native Media Segments & Docker Playback Hardening

This release improves Jellyfin-native skip controls, managed-library refresh behavior, authentication visibility, and Docker playback safety. It also expands automated coverage and adds formatting/analyzer checks to both stable and nightly release pipelines.

### Licensing and Branding
- The repository is now licensed for non-commercial use under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0**.
- Added explicit commercial licensing, trademark, and required-notice documents.
- Commercial use requires separate permission from the project owner; the AniLiberty STRM name and branding are not granted for unrestricted reuse.

### Docker Direct Play Guard
- Fixed automatic playback proxy URL selection inside Docker and other containers.
- The plugin no longer writes container-only bridge addresses such as `172.17.x.x` into generated `.strm` files.
- Proxy base URL priority is now: explicit **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL**, `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl`, then native-host auto-detection outside containers.
- When no client-reachable HTTP(S) base URL exists in a container, generation safely falls back to direct AniLiberty HLS URLs and records a clear task warning.
- Invalid manual or published proxy URLs are ignored instead of producing broken playback links.

### Native Skip Intro / Outro
- Replaced generated EDL and chapter XML skip files with a Jellyfin `IMediaSegmentProvider` implementation.
- Opening and ending timings are stored in `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/media-segments.json` and exposed as native Jellyfin media segments.
- Added background warm-up and path-to-episode reconciliation so existing library items receive updated skip timings without rewriting user-authored metadata.

### Managed Mirror and Metadata Refresh
- Expanded managed manifest tracking for STRM, NFO, artwork, popularity metadata, and media-segment state.
- Generated metadata is refreshed when the upstream AniLiberty signal changes while unmarked user-authored files remain protected.
- Cleanup remains bounded to plugin-managed files, with `Keep`, `DryRun`, and opt-in `Delete` behavior.
- Improved specials, franchise-season, fractional-ordinal, hydration, and image-handling paths.

### Popularity and Authentication Visibility
- Added an optional AniLiberty popularity badge to Jellyfin Web item pages.
- Added a public, read-only metadata endpoint backed only by plugin-generated popularity sidecars.
- Added Jellyfin activity notifications when a stored AniLiberty token starts returning HTTP 401/403, with cooldown protection against notification spam.
- Improved login/password, OTP, favorites, and watch-timecode API handling and validation.

### Playback and Sync Reliability
- Kept HLS playlist and segment delivery streaming through Jellyfin without buffering complete media objects in memory.
- Improved STRM URL normalization, playlist route handling, redirect validation, and playback diagnostics.
- Improved per-session watch-progress coordination, cancellation, path resolution, and forward-only progress updates.

### Quality Gates and Verification
- Added `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` to stable and nightly workflows, covering formatting and built-in Roslyn analyzer diagnostics without an extra linter dependency.
- Expanded automated coverage across controllers, API clients, scheduled tasks, managed cleanup, native media segments, popularity injection, authentication notifications, and Docker proxy URL selection.
- Full release-gated result: **207/207 non-integration tests passed**, clean Debug and Release builds, and zero compiler warnings. Three opt-in live AniLiberty API checks remain outside the release gate.
- Reproduced the Docker failure on Jellyfin 10.11.11: an internal bridge URL caused `DirectPlayError` and ffmpeg fallback; a client-reachable proxy URL played the same H.264/AAC stream through Direct Play with no transcoding.

### Upgrade Notes
- Restart Jellyfin after installing the update.
- Run **Generate AniLiberty STRM library** again so existing `.strm` files and managed state receive the new routing and metadata behavior.
- Docker users who want Jellyfin-proxied playback should set **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL** or `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl` to an address reachable by playback devices and the Jellyfin container.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No full-segment server-side cache or mid-segment resume; brief client-side HLS buffering remains the current protection against connection jitter.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts or the legacy GitHub Pages repository URL.
- No season-gap fix: the reported missing-season case was not established as a plugin defect in this work.

Release 2.0.0.11
AniLiberty STRM Support Trace & Docker Preflight

This update adds a safer diagnostics flow for Docker and headless Jellyfin setups: compact logs stay readable, while the Support Trace rail captures the full failure context needed for issue triage.

### Diagnostic Command Center
- Added a **Huge trace** switch for explicit support sessions.
- `Show logs` now remains the compact operational view for normal task results.
- `Show support trace` exposes the high-volume diagnostic stream only after Huge trace is enabled and the task is rerun.
- `Copy support bundle` packages sanitized configuration, compact logs, and captured support trace without exposing AniLiberty tokens.

### Full Exception Visibility
- Support trace now records full exception details, including stack traces and inner exceptions.
- Compact logs keep short, readable error summaries so normal UI logging does not turn into a wall of text.
- Verified with a read-only Docker output path: the trace captures the filesystem failure, plugin preflight stack, task failure stack, and remediation hint.

### Docker Output Flight Check
- Scheduled generation now validates that the configured output root is writable before fetching AniLiberty catalog data.
- Permission and path failures now stop early with a clear message about Docker volume mapping, host directory ownership, and PUID/PGID permissions.
- Favorites and full-catalog generation both run this preflight before network/catalog work begins.

### Noise Suppression
- Detailed catalog page progress, per-title generation chatter, and stale-file dry-run lists are routed into support trace instead of compact logs.
- Compact logging defaults remain tuned for routine operation.
- Debug logging in compact logs is now described separately from support trace so the UI makes the diagnostic path clearer.

### Verification
- Built and tested with the non-integration suite.
- Smoke-tested in Docker on Jellyfin 10.11 with manifest installation.
- Confirmed support trace captures full write-permission failures while compact logs remain short.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No change to the legacy repository URL used for the plugin manifest.

Release 2.0.0.10
AniLiberty STRM Docker Playback Rail Fix

This update tightens the Docker playback path for AniLiberty STRM Plugin and documents the supported container workflow: repository manifest install, container-visible output path, scheduled reconstruction, Jellyfin library scan, and proxied HLS playback.

### Docker Playback Proxy Rail
- Fixed a Docker/headless Jellyfin case where `ReverseVirtualPath` could resolve the playback proxy route as `file:///AniLibertyPlayback/hls`.

Release 2.0.0.9
AniLiberty STRM Hardening System Release

This update hardens AniLiberty STRM Plugin as a full Jellyfin reconstruction system: stable Jellyfin ABI targeting, explicit AniLiberty identity, safer generated-library governance, streaming playback proxying, and a stronger operational surface for administrators.

### Jellyfin Compatibility & Quality Gates
- Pinned all `Jellyfin.*` NuGet references to `10.11.0` to stop builds from silently drifting to newer Jellyfin packages.
- Added committed `packages.lock.json` files and locked restore in CI.
- Added CI checks that verify every resolved `Jellyfin.*` package remains on `10.11.0` while `targetAbi` stays `10.11.0.0`.
- Release automation now keeps `build.yaml`, package version, assembly version, file version, and informational version in sync.

### AniLiberty Identity & API Courtesy
- Rebranded the public plugin identity to **AniLiberty STRM Plugin** while keeping the legacy `AniLibriaStrmPlugin` repository URL for install compatibility and branch history.
- Added a shared `PluginIdentity` with display name, product token, repository URL, version discovery, and canonical User-Agent.
- All AniLiberty API, media proxy, static media, and HLS clients now identify as:
  `AniLibertyStrmPlugin/<version> (Jellyfin; +https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin)`.

### Mirror Governance Layer
- Added `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/manifest.json` inside each output root to track files managed by the plugin.
- The manifest records generated STRM, ANIID, EDL, chapter XML, NFO, artwork/thumbs, release/episode IDs, hashes, sources, and timestamps.
- First manifest run initializes the baseline and never prunes existing files.
- Generated NFO/artwork refreshes only when the file is known as plugin-managed through the manifest or generated marker.
- Existing unmarked `.nfo` files and artwork are preserved as user-owned content.

### Safe Cleanup Modes
- Added `StaleCleanupMode`: `Off`, `DryRun`, and `Delete`.
- Default is `DryRun`, which reports stale managed files without deleting anything.
- `Delete` removes only manifest-managed stale files and then removes empty directories created by that cleanup path.
- Untracked user files are left alone.

### Playback Proxy Rail
- Non-playlist HLS segments and keys now stream directly to `Response.Body`.
- The proxy no longer reads segment/key payloads into memory with `ReadAsByteArrayAsync`.
- Upstream host allow-listing and redirect validation remain in place.
- Playlist rewriting continues to route segments and keys through the Jellyfin proxy endpoint.

### Identity & Access Command Center
- OTP codes are no longer persisted in plugin configuration after the OTP flow.
- Login/password and OTP sign-in clear stored OTP state.
- The token box is masked by default, with explicit reveal/copy actions.
- Auth logs no longer include the login e-mail address.

### Operational Reliability
- Scheduled tasks now rethrow failures after logging so Jellyfin can mark task execution accurately.
- Cancellation flows are preserved instead of being swallowed as generic failures.
- AniLiberty progress pull no longer overwrites newer local Jellyfin playback positions with older remote timecodes.
- Clearing UI logs now persists the cleared state.

### Presentation & Documentation
- README now presents the plugin as a coherent product system: Signal Acquisition Layer, Context-Aware Reconstruction Core, Playback Proxy Rail, Mirror Governance Layer, Operational Command Center, and Distribution Quality Gates.
- Added three README visual assets showing the reconstruction core, system capability layers, and operational command center.

### Test Coverage
- Added tests for Jellyfin package pins and lock-file resolution.
- Added User-Agent and named/static HTTP client coverage.
- Added managed mirror tests for baseline creation, generated metadata refresh, unmarked NFO preservation, dry-run cleanup, delete cleanup, and empty-directory cleanup.
- Added proxy tests for streaming segments, playlist rewriting, unsupported upstream rejection, redirect validation, and upstream failure status.
- Added auth/config tests for OTP payload boundaries, safe defaults, and AniLiberty identity.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build in this release.
- No migration of AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No destructive cleanup unless `StaleCleanupMode` is explicitly changed to `Delete`.

# AniLiberty API v1 Alignment, Better Metadata & Quieter Logs

This update improves AniLiberty authentication reliability, aligns the plugin with AniLiberty API v1 responses, and enhances generated metadata while keeping UI logs under control.

## Authentication & OTP
- Improved login and OTP endpoints with proper HTTP status codes and safer request validation.
- Updated OTP parsing to support the API v1 format (`otp.code`) and kept backward compatibility for older responses.
- OTP flow in the settings UI is simplified to **Start → Sign In** (the “Accept OTP” UI action was removed).

## Networking reliability
- Switched API calls to a reusable, DI-managed `HttpClient` (`IHttpClientFactory`) with consistent headers (User-Agent / Accept / Accept-Language).
- Added retry handling for rate limits (**HTTP 429**) and transient errors.
- Optimized HTTP reads using `ResponseHeadersRead` to reduce overhead and improve responsiveness.

## STRM generation & metadata quality
- Better year handling for AniLiberty v1 (`release.year` instead of `season.year`), including TV show year selection across grouped seasons.
- More accurate content classification:
  - Detects **MOVIE** by API `type.value` when available.
  - Routes **SPECIAL / OVA / OAD** into **Season 00** more reliably.
- Improved image handling:
  - Supports v1 image schema (`preview/thumbnail/optimized`) and prefers non-optimized URLs when possible.
  - Normalizes `.webp` URLs to `.jpg` and safely determines thumbnail file extensions even when URLs contain query parameters.
- Episode NFO improvements:
  - Writes episode titles (RU/EN when available), runtime, year, and sets `lockdata=false`.

## Logging & settings
- Added **“Enable debug logs (very noisy)”** setting:
  - When OFF: DEBUG/TRACE aren’t stored in UI logs and per-title progress logging is throttled to avoid bloating the UI log.
- UI log filtering now respects minimum log level and the debug toggle.

## Developer / maintenance
- Manual generation test is now **skipped by default** and uses environment variables (`ANI_TOKEN`, `ANI_OUTPUT_DIR`) so tokens aren’t stored in the repo.
- Internal null-safety improvements around plugin initialization.

## Not included
- No changes to library scanning behavior or broader UI redesign beyond the OTP/auth/logging settings shown above.
